Welcome toThe Butts Primary School
The Butts is a popular community school, where children thrive because they feel happy and safe to develop the independence that they need to move forward with confidence in a rapidly changing world.
We work in close partnership with parents and the community and the needs of the children are always our primary consideration. We believe in educating the 'whole child' and, during their time with us, the children will enjoy an interesting and wide ranging curriculum.
Why Choose Our School?
We will nurture children and help them to develop socially, emotionally, academically, culturally, creatively, physically and spiritually.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Butts Primary School - Attendance and Absence Procedures
pageCache.text:
Attendance and Absence Procedures
Good attendance at school is directly linked to progress and attainment. At The Butts Primary School, we pride ourselves on excellent attendance figures.
If your child is going to be absent from school due to illness, please notify us by 9am in any of the following ways:
Please ensure that you let us know the name of your child, their class / year group the nature of the illness (including symptoms) and the likely duration of absence. This is particularly important if your child has symptoms of COVID-19 and is required to self-isolate.
Parents are sometimes unsure whether to keep children off school and you may find the guidance in the attached leaflet helpful.
Please note that if your child has a diarrhoea or sickness they will need to remain off school for 48 hours after the last episode of vomiting or diarrhoea.
You will also need to phone the school on each day of absence.
Where possible, please try to avoid school hours when booking routine medical, dental, optician and hospital appointments. We do understand that this is not always possible, in which case please let us know in advance so that we can let the relevant members of staff know.
Parents are requested not to take family holidays during school term-time. If you do wish to take your child out of school during term-time you will need to request permission by completing and submitting this form prior to the period of intended absence.
Headteachers are only able to authorise absence from school in exceptional circumstances and when making a request for authorised absence from school, you will need to explain why the circumstances are exceptional. Please note that there is general right to authorise absence for a family holiday. If you take your child out of school without permission, the absence will be recorded as unauthorised and this may result in a Penalty Notice being issued. The attached leaflet gives further details.
If your child is absent from school and we do not hear from you by 9.15am, we will send you a text message asking you to contact us urgently and let us know the reason for the absence. If we do not receive a response within 30 minutes we will telephone you. If we are unable to contact you by telephone, we will phone other named contacts that you have given us until we are able to establish the reasons for absence and that your child is safe. In the event that we are unable to make contact and we are concerned for the safety and well-being of your child, we may contact the police or social services.
Promoting Good Attendance
If your child’s attendance over the year falls below 90%, you will receive a letter from the school. Further falls in attendance will prompt further warning letters and you will be invited in to discuss your child’s attendance with the Headteacher. If attendance still does not improve, you may face fines or Court action in line with Hampshire Policy (see link)
Please ensure that your child arrives on time for school each day. Pupils who arrive after registers have closed at 8.50am must sign in at the school office. Please note that late marks count as missed sessions (absences) on your child’s attendance record even if they are only 5 minutes late.
The following links provide further information regarding the school’s approach to attendance at school:

pageCache.pageTitle: The Butts Primary School - Breakfast Club
pageCache.text:
Breakfast Club
We are pleased to be able to offer a Breakfast Club at The Butts Primary School, where your child will receive a warm welcome and a hearty breakfast from Mrs Barnes or Mrs Ratcliffe. There is always cereal and toast available, together with a hot option. Please see below for an example of the choices which may be available.
Breakfast Club Sample Menu
Breakfast Club runs from 7.45am until 8.40am every day and is based in the Music Room. We would ask that you drop your child off at the external door to the Music Room, rather than via the School Office, so that they can be registered and any messages passed on to the staff.
The cost is £5 per session.
We do request that, where possible, places are booked in advance although we do understand that plans sometimes change at short notice.
Payment and booking is made using the Scopay system. We do accept payment using Childcare Vouchers and from Tax-Free Childcare accounts. For further details, please contact Mrs Speller in the School Office.

pageCache.text:
Learning Resources
English
Oxford Owl Library-Please sign up to Oxford Owl to have access to the free e-book library.
Audible-all children’s audiobooks are available for free while schools are closed.
Literacy Shed– downloadable resource packs with tasks based on video clips on YouTube.
The Children’s Poetry Archive-an archive of spoken poetry recordings. Children can listen to poems read out loud.
Maths
Hamilton Trust-downloadable resource packs with teacher guidance. A week’s worth of resources is provided for each year group.
Mathematics Mastery-downloadable guidance and resource packs for parents and pupils.
Nrich-a range of activities. Some are interactive and some are to be completed offline. Activities are categorised by age range.
Numberblocks-ideas for numeracy development designed for children aged 0 to 6. There are fun activities that can be applied to everyday life and play.
Topmarks-a range of interactive maths games categorised by age group.
White Rose Maths-presentations and downloadable workbooks which are easy to use for parents. New material is being released each week.
Science
BBC Bitesize-interactive resources covering the primary science curriculum.
STEM Learning-an online resource bank, which links to resources on external websites. The site features a live chat function offering support from subject experts. New home learning resources are being developed.
PE
Disney 10 Minute Shakeups-10-minute activities based on Disney films that count towards a child’s 60 active minutes per day.
SuperMovers– videos which help children move while they learn. They support curriculum subjects, including maths and English.
Mental Well-Being
British Psychology Society (BPS)-advice on dealing with school closures and talking to children about COVID-19.
MindEd-an educational resource for all adults on children and young people’s mental health

pageCache.pageTitle: The Butts Primary School - Meet our Governors
pageCache.text:
Meet our Governors
The current members of our Governing Body are:
Abi Legg - Chair of Governors
My name is Abi Legg and I am the Chair of Governors at The Butts Primary School. I have been a secondary school teacher for 14 years and when my eldest child started in Reception a parent governor role came up on The Butts Governors Board. With my experience in education, I felt this was an area I could "give back" to my child's school and our local area.
I thoroughly enjoy the role - from regular visits to school to our Full Governor Board meetings, I feel able to support and contribute to our brilliant, ambitious local school.
The key role of the Governing Body is to provide a blend of support and challenge to the school`s leaders. We work with the Headteacher and leadership team to make sure the school has a clear vision for the future, understands what and how it can improve and provides the very best education and learning experiences to all. In addition to our strategic role we aim to develop strong links between the School and the community it serves.
The Governors are individuals (10 in all by constitution) with widely different skills and backgrounds. They include members of the local community, parents, a Local Authority nominee, a staff representative and the Headteacher. We work as a team, united by a passion to ensure that all the children reach their full potential.
As a Governing Body, we are as open as possible about all decisions and actions we take. We welcome direct contact with any member of the wider school community. If you need to contact me about a school matter, please drop me a line via the school office.
Carol Whitehouse - Community Governor
My name is Carol Whitehouse and I am the link Governor for SEN and lead KS1. I have worked as a medical secretary to Dr. H Angelman, a Consultant Paediatrician, who discovered Angelman syndrome. Later I trained as a Primary School Teacher and on retiring I studied at Helen Arkell, gaining the OCR Diploma in Teaching Learners with Dyslexia/Specific Learning Difficulties. The early years of a child’s life are a vital period in a person’s life and it is up to schools to give them the best start. I believe that quality education empowers children and young people, safeguards their health and well-being, and breaks cycles of poverty and temptation into criminal activities. Being a Governor is a way to contribute locally, and to society as a whole, by helping to improve children’s education, opportunities, and futures: and also, to make this a happy time in their life!
Chris Lee - Parent Governor
I am Chris, parent governor and link for English writing, sport, health and safety and I’ve recently taken on attendance lead. I have been RAF aircrew for 20 years now, 11 of those flying on Chinooks out of Odiham so apologies if you’ve been woken up at stupid o’clock by the aggressive noise. My job has taken me away for long periods, so knowing my child had a safe, stable network at the Butts took some of the pressure off. Becoming a governor allows me to take a small part in making sure the school continues to provide it’s excellent service to all the children who attend.
Louis Ward - Parent Governor
My name is Louis Ward and I am a parent governor and link governor for maths and the school's finances. I have a legal background and currently work for a financial services firm. When the opportunity came up to become a parent governor, I jumped at the chance to contribute in whatever way I can to the continued excellence of the school and to provide the best possible learning environment for all children who attend.
Helena Lewis - Parent Governor
As a local grandmother spending many an afternoon at the school on collection duty, I have become familiar with The Butts over the past few years and have always been impressed by the happy and relaxed atmosphere around the children and staff. Being a retired lady of a 'certain age' I am able to help out with the daytime duties of a school governor whilst hopefully contributing to the role through my past career experience in management, local government and as a school governors' clerk at primary level in Hampshire.
Georgette Page - Staff Governor
I have worked at The Butts for over 6 years, with experience in EYFS and both Key Stages. Both of my children also went through the school, so I feel I have got a good overview of all aspects of the school both as a parent and a member of the team. I am deeply loyal to our school and only want the best for our children and staff, which is why I became a staff Governor.
Hazel Cantoni - Community Governor
BEd, main subject Geography with education for 3 - 9 year olds.
Taught for 34 years in Infant and Primary schools including mixed age groups in a village school and latterly as part of the senior leadership team. Taught French throughout the Primary phase (my accent remains very English I’m afraid!) Also spent 4 (I think!) years working as Teacher in charge of an annexe to a Send school, working with the most severely compromised children.
Teamwork, leadership skills, communication skills dealing with various agencies including physiotherapists and parents and children, adaptability with plan a,b and c when working in a small school and creativity. Used many of the above skills when organising things at Alton Rugby Club, Mothers and Toddlers, PTA and as a volunteer for HIOWAA and St Michaels Hospice. Interested in all aspects of school life including Early Years, creative projects and sport.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Butts Primary School - Music Lessons
pageCache.text:
Music Lessons
As part of our music curriculum, pupils in Year 4 take part in a ‘Listen2Me’ programme, provided by the Hampshire Music Service. Children learn a variety of instruments in a whole class setting, such as keyboard, ukelele, samba drums and violin. The instrument changes on a termly basis.
In addition to our class music curriculum, The Butts Primary School is able to provide peripatetic music tuition for children in Years 3, 4, 5 and 6 through Hampshire Music Service. Children are taught mostly in small groups, promoting ensemble skills which can prepare them for joining a band or orchestra should they so wish. Lessons can be provided in brass, woodwind, strings and guitar. An annual charge applies, which can be paid either in one amount at the start of the academic year or in termly instalments. Instruments are available to hire through Hampshire Music Service, so there is no need to purchase any instruments if you do not wish to. Parents and pupils must commit to music lessons for the whole academic year.
If you are interested in signing your child up for peripatetic music tuition, please contact the School Office for more information.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Butts Primary School - Our Governors
pageCache.text:
Our Governors
The Butts governing board - bringing people together
The Butts Primary School has a dedicated team of Governors. Some are community governors, appointed by the governing board and some are elected by Parents. We have one staff member elected by staff and one governor nominated by the Local Authority Governor. The Headteacher is also a member of the governing board. All Governors serve a four year term.
All governors are members of the Full Governing Body (FGB) and meet collectively nine times in an academic year. The FGB works closely with the Headteacher to set the aims and objectives for the school and set the policies and targets for achieving those aims. They monitor the progress the school is making towards these achievements and provide a source of challenge and support to the Headteacher.
Each governor on the board has a specific responsibility, eg: Safeguarding; Health and Safety; Teaching and Learning; Finance; Special Educational Needs and Disability. In this way, we assist and challenge both the curricular and financial aspects of the school’s development and the School Improvement Plan.
The current membership of the Governing Board is shown on the attached document.
Further details about all of our Governors can be found on our Meet our Governors page
Vacancies for Governors sometimes arise and we’d love to hear from anybody who would like to join us in this important work.
We do currently have a vacancy for a Community Governor. Please contact the Chair of Governors if you are interested in becoming a Governor.

pageCache.text:
PE and Sports Funding
We recognise that physical activity has numerous benefits for children and young people’s physical health, as well as their mental wellbeing (increasing self-esteem and emotional wellbeing and lowering anxiety and depression), and that children who are physically active are happier, more resilient and more trusting of their peers.
The Butts Primary School prides itself on promoting a range of activities through the taught curriculum, extra-curricular activities and visits, which promote an active lifestyle. Our Primary PE and Sport Premium Funding enables us to continue and enhance our provision through the development of a varied and high-quality PE curriculum, a wider variety of opportunities for participation in competitive sport and extra-curricular activities. The attached documents explain how we have used our PE and Sport Premium Funding over the recent academic years.
